subject: leopard
title: One Leopard Hunts a Cave of 40,000 Bats, Up to 40 in a Night

scenes.text: One leopard found a meal that flies straight past its nose.
Python Cave in Uganda holds around 40,000 Egyptian fruit bats.
Hidden cameras watched the entrance for months. At least ten kinds of animals came to eat them.
Blue monkeys, crowned eagles and Nile monitor lizards all took their share.
But the leopard was the regular. A researcher saw it eat 30 or 40 bats in one night.
Those bats carry Marburg virus. So every hunter at that cave is a clue to how it spreads.

description:
Camera traps at Python Cave in Queen Elizabeth National Park, Uganda, home to around 40,000 Egyptian fruit bats, filmed at least ten species eating or scavenging the bats (Current Biology, 2026).
Blue monkeys, crowned eagles, Nile monitors and a leopard that sometimes ate 30 to 40 bats a night all visited. The bats are a known reservoir of Marburg virus, and more than 200 people were also filmed at the cave.
Which predator surprised you most?
first_comment: The cameras also filmed more than 200 human visitors at the same cave. Would you go in?
